_doc: The voice cast sheet (UPDATE 06 B1, T-101). characters.<game>.<code>.actor = the actor id voicing that character (a list for a group, e.g. the Cousins together); "[ACTOR]" / "[COUSIN_1]" are unfilled placeholders (each still gets its own script as slot_<code>). One actor can voice several characters: give them the same id. actors.<id>: name (shown on the script), contact (optional, never shown), notes. Actor ids are lowercase (voice_inbox/<id>/, voice_scripts/<id>/). Read by tools/voice/make_scripts.py and tools/voice/import.py. Edit this file, then run tools/voice.sh scripts.

DUT.name: Sgt. Walter "Dutch" Kowalczyk
DUT.who: Sgt. Dutch Kowalczyk, 34, Pittsburgh: low, gravelly baritone, unhurried, complains to keep going
DUT.voice_notes: Low, gravelly baritone. Pittsburgh vowels ("dahntahn," "yinz" exactly once per map, never more). Unhurried, even in a crisis. / His default register is complaint. He complains the way other men pray: steadily, to keep going. He is never actually panicking. When he goes quiet, the squad worries. / His Polish is kitchen Polish learned from an old woman: wrong genders, wrong cases, a grandmother's accent. Read it confidently and wrong. Wren corrects him; he never learns. / Softens noticeably around Wren. Talks to the dead Gängers like disappointed relatives.

PEG.name: Lt. Margaret "Peg" Ashworth
PEG.who: Lt. Peg Ashworth, 29, SOE: Received Pronunciation, clipped and precise, never raises her voice
PEG.voice_notes: Received Pronunciation, clipped, precise. Never raises her voice. The worse things get, the more politely she speaks. In a crisis she sounds bored. / Sardonic understatement is her armor: a horde is "a spot of bother." She swears rarely, and when she does it's devastating. / When she's lying, she gets *more* precise, not less. The actor should play the LANTERN hints as tiny, nearly invisible pauses. / Professional fascination with explosives, said with unsettling warmth.

DEA.name: Cpl. Elijah "Deacon" Brooks
DEA.who: Cpl. Deacon Brooks, 26, Louisiana: warm tenor, soft-spoken, a preacher's rhythm
DEA.voice_notes: Warm Louisiana tenor, soft-spoken, with a preacher's sense of rhythm he inherited and resists. When he gets going, he can't help preaching a little and then catches himself. / Talks to machines like livestock: "Easy now, girl," "Come on, mule." Never condescending to people. / His blues lines are his own, half-sung, made up on the spot. They should sound like real field blues: AAB form, plain words, bent notes. / Quietly funny. His jokes land half a beat late and he enjoys them more than anyone.

WRN.name: Zofia "Wren" Nowak
WRN.who: Wren (Zofia Nowak), 24, Home Army: fluent English learned from British radio, a Polish accent, economical and deadpan
WRN.voice_notes: A Polish speaker with fluent but accented English (learned from British radio and an SOE liaison). Clipped, economical, never wasted words. / Dark humor delivered completely deadpan. She doesn't laugh at her own jokes. / Precise about numbers. She counts out loud under her breath: "sześćdziesiąt dwa... sześćdziesiąt trzy." / Fury runs under everything. It surfaces rarely and frighteningly, mostly about the lab, the tanks, and the forced laborers. / Softens only with Dutch, whom she treats like an embarrassing uncle.

OPR.name: The Operator
OPR.who: A sampled 1930s radio announcer on the mine's tannoy: bright, brassy, a little too quick and too cheerful; sometimes the cold corporate voice of the Ledger leaks through.
OPR.voice_notes: Play it like a vintage radio host who is slightly wrong. The radio effect is added afterwards: record it clean.

JAK.name: Jakub Ostrowski
JAK.who: Jakub Ostrowski, 44, Silesian salt hewer: English learned late and well enough, an older Polish voice, calm and wry
JAK.voice_notes: Calm, wry, polite. Slow, careful English learned from a German foreman and Polish newspapers; Polish when it matters (shouting, praying, his wife's name), always with the English beside it in the subtitle. / He has seen worse than zombies and isn't impressed by them. Dry humour about himself, never about the dead. / Never raises his voice except at the breakout. Under fire he stays steady.

FAS.name: Dr. Emil Fasbender
FAS.who: A scientist in his mid-40s, nervous and rapid, always speaking with his hand over the radio mic.
FAS.voice_notes: Fast, whispered urgency. The field-radio effect is added afterwards: record it clean.

REI.name: Dr. Augusta Reinholt
REI.who: Early 50s, cultured, controlled and slow; heard on old wax-cylinder recordings and hijacking the PA.
REI.voice_notes: Cold precision; warmer on the cylinders (her diary). The phonograph / PA effects are added afterwards.

LSL.name: Liesl
LSL.who: Reinholt's daughter, seven, heard on her mother's wax cylinders.
LSL.voice_notes: A child playing; innocent. If no child voices her, an adult can play it lightly. Phonograph effect added afterwards.

WIE.name: Konrad Wiesner
WIE.who: Konrad Wiesner, a railway signalman (50s) walking home to Hirschfelde, at Verdun in 1916: steady and weary, a deep roughened voice; English as a careful second language, a German accent (T-077)
WIE.voice_notes: A real person speaking English as a careful second language: a light German accent, played straight, never comic.

BRA.name: Fraeulein Hedwig Brandt
BRA.who: Fraeulein Hedwig Brandt, the schoolteacher at Hirschfelde (30s): brisk and frightened, a clear precise voice, a German accent (T-077)
BRA.voice_notes: A real person speaking English as a careful second language: a light German accent, played straight, never comic.

KRO.name: Ida Kroll
KRO.who: Ida Kroll, the postwoman from Sankt Anna (20s): quick and talkative when scared, a young bright voice, a light German accent (T-077)
KRO.voice_notes: A real person speaking English as a careful second language: a light German accent, played straight, never comic.

SOB.name: Gefreiter Willi Sobotta
SOB.who: Gefreiter Willi Sobotta, a lance-corporal on Christmas leave (20): a young soldier trying to sound steady, a light German accent
SOB.voice_notes: A real person speaking English as a careful second language: a light German accent, played straight, never comic.

ROT.name: Ewald Rother
ROT.who: Ewald Rother, an old Silesian salt carter (60s): gruff and kind, a deep worn voice, slow; English as a careful second language, a German accent
ROT.voice_notes: A real person speaking English as a careful second language: a light German accent, played straight, never comic.

KUB.name: Franz Kubiak
KUB.who: Franz Kubiak, Rother's younger mate (20s): quick and frightened, a lighter voice, a light German accent
KUB.voice_notes: A real person speaking English as a careful second language: a light German accent, played straight, never comic.

TRU.name: Trudi Hanke
TRU.who: Trudi Hanke, a farmer's daughter (20s) helping at the bar: practical and loud, a bright warm voice, a light German accent
TRU.voice_notes: A real person speaking English as a careful second language: a light German accent, played straight, never comic.

POH.name: Frau Agnes Pohl
POH.who: Frau Agnes Pohl, a widow (50s) walking to her sister's in Liegnitz: prim and proper, an older woman's voice, a German accent
POH.voice_notes: A real person speaking English as a careful second language: a light German accent, played straight, never comic.

HAM.name: The Hammer (Mara)
HAM.who: young woman, about 22 (the eldest); Blonde hair; carries a mallet she throws. Throws the mallet like a boomerang and catches it
HAM.voice_notes: Creepy-doll horror, playful and sad, never sexualized. Lines are German with the English in brackets: say the German. A subtle eerie room reverb is added afterwards.

RCH.name: The Reach (Jo)
RCH.who: young woman, about 18 (the youngest); Brown hair; extremely long arms. Reaching: grabs things far away, through windows and floors
RCH.voice_notes: Creepy-doll horror, playful and sad, never sexualized. Lines are German with the English in brackets: say the German. A subtle eerie room reverb is added afterwards.

ALX.name: The Third Hand (Alix)
ALX.who: young woman, about 20; An arm that extends out of her torso; double damage. The arm is 'the hand she was always holding'
ALX.voice_notes: Creepy-doll horror, playful and sad, never sexualized. Lines are German with the English in brackets: say the German. A subtle eerie room reverb is added afterwards.

CSN.name: The Cousins (together)
CSN.who: All three cousins at once: the rhyme hummed and whispered, the trio lines.
CSN.voice_notes: Each cousin records these; the importer layers the takes into a trio (one take alone is doubled).

PAUL.name: PAUL (homage boss)
PAUL.who: A homage boss based on the owner's friend Paul. Not in the game yet: no lines.

SLENDER.name: THE SLENDER (homage boss)
SLENDER.who: A homage boss voiced by the owner. Not in the game yet: no lines.

SQD.name: Relief squad soldiers (T-142)
SQD.who: Soldiers of seven relief squads who walk in from the map edge (UPDATE 09 section 4): Home Army partisans (SQD_AK), a Red Army scout (SQD_SOV), Volkssturm deserters, old men (SQD_VS), British commandos (SQD_CDO), a Kriegsmarine rating (SQD_KM), a US paratrooper (SQD_PARA), a Groom Lake MP (SQD_MP).
SQD.voice_notes: One voice per faction, each a real person under fire: English with the odd word of their own language, accents light and played straight, never comic; the Volkssturm old men with dignity.

sprocket.name: Sprocket
sprocket.who: Bolt's robot sidekick: dry, smug, very fast. A light robot treatment is added afterwards: record it clean, in your own voice.
